response.title: what should i buy to run a window air conditioner during a summer outage
response.answer:
To run a window air conditioner during a summer power outage, I'd recommend buying either a portable inverter generator or a large LiFePO4 battery power station, depending on whether you can safely operate a generator outdoors.

The biggest consideration is that air conditioners consume much more electricity than phones, lights, or refrigerators. A typical window AC can drain a $1,000 battery in just a few hours.

What size backup power do you need?

Here are approximate power requirements for common window AC units.

Window AC size

10,000 BTU

6.4–9.6 kWh




12,000 BTU

	

1,000–1,500 W

	

8–12 kWh

These estimates assume continuous operation. Actual consumption depends on the model, outdoor temperature, thermostat setting, and compressor cycling.

For example, an 8,000 BTU air conditioner averaging 700 W would require approximately 6–7 kWh of battery capacity for eight hours, after accounting for inverter losses.

Important safety considerations

A gasoline generator must operate outdoors, at least 20 feet from the house, with exhaust directed away from openings. Never operate it in a garage, even with the door open. Use working carbon monoxide alarms.

+1

For a window AC, check the manufacturer’s extension-cord instructions. Avoid extension cords where prohibited; otherwise use a properly rated, grounded cord. Never connect a generator to household wiring without a professionally installed transfer switch.

        <radio value="10000">10,000 BTU</radio>

      </radio-group>
    </box>
    <divider color="subtle"/>
    <box gap={1}>
      <label>2. How long must it run without utility power?</label>
      <radio-group direction="col" value={duration} onChange={setDuration}>

        <radio value="8">8 hours</radio>
        <radio value="12">12 hours</radio>
        <radio value="24">24 hours or longer</radio>
      </radio-group>
    </box>
    <divider color="subtle"/>
    <box gap={1}>
      <label>3. Do you have a safe outdoor space for a generator?</label>
      <radio-group direction="col" value={outdoor} onChange={setOutdoor}>
        <radio value="yes">Yes — detached outdoor area</radio>
        <radio value="no">No — need an indoor battery solution</radio>
      </radio-group>
    </box>
    <button submit block>Find my best backup power setup <icon name="arrow-right" inline/></button>
  </form>
</box>

These answers will help determine whether a $1,000-class generator is sufficient or whether you need a larger battery system costing several thousand dollars.
